message.content: monokl: implement the new default output shape measured in the output-economics sweep (summary): default output median is 10 KB, rows past rank 3 hold 91% of bytes and only 6% of questions have their answer there; snippet is 50% of each row; 58% of bytes past rank 3 are same-file repeats. Measured recommendation: default 1 snippet line and a relevance cut: keep rows with finalScore >= 0.3 x the top score, always keep at least 3 rows (if that many exist) and at most 15 (then the cap wins). On the 222-row harness: median bytes 10,012 -> 904, p90 13,351 -> 3,189, one-turn answerable 216 -> 213 (<=1 question lost per set; snippet 0 is NOT acceptable: variable/type rows have no signature). Cut from #105's branch (it changes snippet and row selection that #105/#107 touched): `git fetch origin && git switch -c feat/lean-default-output origin/feat/span-hit-ownership`; if #105 has merged into main by the time you finish, merge origin/main and retarget. Build: (1) default snippet lines 1 (a `--snippet-lines N` flag, 0..=3 or whatever the current max is, N=3 restores today's snippets; reject 0? keep 0 allowed but document that variable/type rows lose their declaration text); (2) the relevance cut as default with a flag `--min-score FRACTION` (0 disables the cut; default 0.3) and keep `--max-results` as the cap (default 15 when the cut is on? check the current default row cap and how `--max-tokens` interacts; state the final rule in docs); (3) the truncation/help line must name the flag: when rows were cut by the relevance rule or the cap, the help says e.g. `showing 4 of 37; --min-score 0 or --max-results N for more, or refine with +term/-term` — use michi's hint machinery, do not hand-roll; counts only in core (items_returned/items_total), the output layer renders the text (AGENTS.md non-negotiable); (4) no `--offset` for now (note it as a known gap in docs, don't build it). Core stays free of pre-rendered strings and caps beyond counts. TDD, exact-value tests: the cut rule table (scores, top, floor 3, cap, ties, fewer than 3 rows, top score 0), flag parsing and errors (exit 2), help text names the flag, the default shape for a TS and a Rust fixture query, N=3 snippet parity with today's output (sibling-path parity). Delete code/tests the change makes dead and update every snapshot/expected string only after checking the new output is the intended one (not just different). Verify by exit code: `just lint` (CI pin 1.99.1), `just test`, `just rg-compare` (harness counts the answer in the rows returned: it must not lose more than 1 question per set vs baseline 59/59 identifiers, 17/18 questions, 15/16 members, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out rust 34/36, react-hook-form 14/14 — if the harness passes explicit flags like a large max-results, make sure it exercises the DEFAULT output shape; report how), `just changesets` (minor with **Breaking:** and **Action:** notes: default output changed; how to get the old output), `just bench` (no slowdown >2%), and measure the new median/p90 bytes over the harness (script from PR #109 lives on origin/test/agent-workflow-cost; you may run scripts/agent-cost.py from that branch checked out in a SEPARATE scratch location pointing at your binary, but do NOT commit its files here). Update README (output example), docs/architecture/query-and-ranking.md/output docs and the decision log with this measurement and the rule; keep the spec honest about what was not measured (model correctness, usage-context value of snippet lines 2-3). Git: isolated worktree; never touch `.claude/settings.json`; Conventional Commits; commit messages end with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n`; push; `entire trail link 361 --branch feat/lean-default-output --base <feat/span-hit-ownership while #105 is open, else main>` (never trail create / gh pr create / force-push); `gh pr ready`; PR description (ends with `https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n`) states the base, that it must merge after #105, shows a before/after output for one real query, and the measured table. Network/signing/gh/entire need dangerouslyDisableSandbox. Report <=150 words: PR link, +/-, checks by exit code, measured bytes before/after, harness deltas.

Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; fails below the threshold, which this default owns
coverage threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check, clippy with and without default features, and typos, the same as CI's lint job
lint: typos
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check --strict
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Fails when a duplicated fact disagrees with its owner, e.g. the Callisto pin in the workflows against .prototools
check-drift:
    scripts/check-drift.sh

# Checks a published release is complete and usable, e.g. `just verify-release 0.4.0`. Needs network and gh.
verify-release version:
    scripts/verify-release.sh {{ version }}

# Score search targeting and output size against ripgrep on pinned public repos. Needs network and `rg`; on demand, not part of `just ci`.
rg-compare *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/rg-compare.py {{ args }}

# Time and peak memory of `monokl search` against ripgrep on pinned repos and a stress set. Warm cache; needs network and `rg`; on demand.
bench *args:
    cargo build --release -q
    python3 -I scripts/bench.py {{ args }}

# Block span and parent invariants over the harness repositories in target/rg-compare (`just rg-compare` fills it) or the directories in MONOKL_SPAN_CORPUS; skips with a message when neither exists. On demand.
span-invariants:
    cargo test -p monokl --test span_invariants --release -- --ignored --nocapture

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true

 - **Harness.** Unchanged: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 32/33 and 22/22, held-out rust 34/36.
 - **Open.** ADR 0005 is complete: analyzers emit spans, hits carry match starts, and ownership, snippets and dedup read them. `code` is still stored in every block, so nested blocks duplicate text; a block could slice its text from the file instead.
 
+
+## 45. The harness measures what an agent pays, not only where the answer ranks (2026-11-15)
+
+- **Decision.** `scripts/agent-cost.py` (`just agent-cost [--detail] [--json PATH]`) scores the `rg-compare` rows for cost: 59 sampled identifiers, 18 questions, 16 members, fd (24 rows), the held-out sets and report-only react-hook-form, 222 rows in all. It reuses `rg-compare.py` for repositories, rows, declaration patterns and monokl's file rules, so no row, pin or rule is duplicated. It is report only: a `FAIL` line prints when a set's median monokl bytes exceed its median rg-policy bytes or its answerable-in-one-turn rate is below 0.8, and the exit status stays 0.
+- **monokl, measured.** One `monokl search <words> .` with default caps. Bytes are its stdout, tokens are `ceil(bytes / 3)` (the product's own estimate), turns are 1. The row is answerable when one of the first 3 rows is in the expected file, spans the declaration's line and shows its text. `monokl+read` adds one read turn of the expected block to a row that is not answerable.

(1.0 to 7.0, below), **`final_score = round6(bm25 * name * ntype)`**.
Sorted by `final_score` descending, then file, `line_start`, `line_end`, `node_kind` and `code`; 1-based `rank` is
assigned after the sort.

`name_match_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`) compares the query terms `Q` (repeats counted) with `N`, the distinct tokens of the
block's declared name (`CodeBlock.name`, tokenized like a document, so stop words such as the `use` of `useWatch` and the
`from` of `FromRequestParts` are not tokens): `R` is the share of `Q` found in `N`, `P` the share of `N` found in `Q`.
`name = round6(1 + 2 * (R + P / 2) / 1.5 + 4 * exact)`, where `exact` is 1 when `R == 1` and `P == 1`. So a name that
holds none of the terms gets 1.0, a name that holds all of them and nothing else gets 7.0, and the name that says more than
the query (`validatePrice` for `price`) or less (`parse` for `parse other`) lands between. 1.0 for an empty query and for a
block with no name or a name of only stop words. 05 §42 records why this shape and the variants it beat.

BM25 (`rank/bm25.rs`): `K1 = 1.5`, `B = 0.5`, standard Okapi formula, `round6` to 6dp for
cross-platform f64 stability (`DP = 1_000_000.0`) — keep this rounding.

`node_type_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`): Function 1.5; Class/Method/Constructor 1.4; Interface/Struct
1.3; TypeAlias/Enum 1.2; Variable/Impl 1.1; Property/Field/Macro 1.0; Module 0.9; Other 0.7.

## Dedup and snippets

Both read the byte spans the analyzers fill ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md)); neither reads line numbers or compares text.

`dedup_blocks` (`dedup.rs`) walks the ranked blocks best first and drops a block that shares more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a block already kept in the same file, then renumbers `rank`. The spans of one analyzed file nest or are disjoint, so this drops a block inside a kept block, equal to it, or holding it, and keeps two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`). A member (a block with a `parent`) never duplicates the top-level block that strictly encloses it, in either rank order. A block with an empty span overlaps nothing. A segment tree over the kept spans' ends keeps the walk near-linear (`tests/scaling.rs`).

The snippet (`output/agent.rs`) shows the matched lines of a block, at most three, each cut to 160 characters, with the rest counted. A matched line is left out when its text lies wholly inside the block's `signature_span`, because the signature column already shows it.

## Determinism and bounds

Resolved findings, kept so they are not reopened:

1. **#7 — a bad `regex:` term fails the whole search.** Every term, excluded ones too, compiles before any file is
   read (05 §18).
2. **#9 — total-order tie-break.** The six sort keys above leave no ties, so the order never depends on input order.
3. **#10 — the file walk is sorted by file name**, so the set of files reached under the file ceiling is reproducible.
4. **#11 — resource bounds.** The text search examines at most 100,000 files and keeps counting past it, reads at most
   4 MiB per file and keeps 4096 bytes per line; `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` cut the output; `--timeout` stops
   the work. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md).

Open:

- **#16 — no cap on one term's or the query's length.** `LIMIT = 64` bounds term *count* only. Decide whether a length
  cap is needed, and which error reports it (a sibling to `TooManyTerms`, not a repurposing of it).

## Dedup and snippets

Both read the byte spans the analyzers fill ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md)); neither reads line numbers or compares text.

`dedup_blocks` (`dedup.rs`) walks the ranked blocks best first and drops a block that shares more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a block already kept in the same file, then renumbers `rank`. The spans of one analyzed file nest or are disjoint, so this drops a block inside a kept block, equal to it, or holding it, and keeps two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`). A member (a block with a `parent`) never duplicates the top-level block that strictly encloses it, in either rank order. A block with an empty span overlaps nothing. A segment tree over the kept spans' ends keeps the walk near-linear (`tests/scaling.rs`).

The snippet (`output/agent.rs`) shows the matched lines of a block, at most three, each cut to 160 characters, with the rest counted. A matched line is left out when its text lies wholly inside the block's `signature_span`, because the signature column already shows it.

Resolved findings, kept so they are not reopened:

1. **#7 — a bad `regex:` term fails the whole search.** Every term, excluded ones too, compiles before any file is

2. **#9 — total-order tie-break.** The six sort keys above leave no ties, so the order never depends on input order.
3. **#10 — the file walk is sorted by file name**, so the set of files reached under the file ceiling is reproducible.
4. **#11 — resource bounds.** The text search examines at most 100,000 files and keeps counting past it, reads at most
   4 MiB per file and keeps 4096 bytes per line; `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` cut the output; `--timeout` stops
   the work. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md).

- **#16 — no cap on one term's or the query's length.** `LIMIT = 64` bounds term *count* only. Decide whether a length

## Install


## Try it

Search a directory (the default is the current one):

```
$ monokl search "format price" src/ --max-results 3
search[3]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,rank,finalScore}:
  src/utils/format.ts,1,3,function,null,"function formatCurrency(amount: number, currency: string = 'USD'): string","2: return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency }).format(amount);",1,5.901294
  src/utils/validation.ts,8,12,function,null,"function validatePrice(price: number): ValidationResult","9: if (price < 0) return { valid: false, message: 'Price cannot be negative' };\n10: if (price > 1_000_000) return { valid: false, message: formatCurrency(1_000_000) + ' is the maximum' };",2,4.151139
  src/index.ts,3,3,other,null,null,"3: export { formatCurrency, truncateString } from './utils/format';",3,1.345138
totalCount: 10
help[1]: showing 3 of 10; raise the cap or refine the query with +term or -term
```

Each row is one match: where it is (`file`, `lineStart`, `lineEnd`), what it is (`nodeKind`: function, class, method, interface, type alias and so on), what holds it (`parent`), its signature, the lines in it that matched (`snippet`), and its `rank` and `finalScore`. Output uses [TOON](https://github.com/toon-format/spec), a table format that costs fewer tokens than JSON.

A method, a constructor, or a class property holding an arrow function or a function expression gets a row of its own when it spans three lines or more and its class is declared at the top level of the file or exported. So does a method, getter, setter, or a property holding an arrow function or a function expression, of an object literal that is assigned to a top-level `const`, `let` or `var`, or is the `export default` value, also through `as`, `satisfies` or parentheses. Its `parent` is `class Foo` for a class member and `variable api` for the members of `const api = { ... }` (`other default` for `export default { ... }`), and `nodeKind` is `method`, `constructor` or `property`; `parent` is `null` on every other row. A line that matched inside a member is shown on the member's row only, and the class's or object's row appears when it has a match outside its members, such as its name. Shorter members, members of an anonymous class, of an interface, of an object literal anywhere else (inside a function, a call or `module.exports = { ... }`) and functions nested inside a member are still reached through the row that holds them.

The `snippet` is the lines of the block that matched, each with its line number and cut at 160 characters. It shows up to three, then counts the rest (`...and 2 more matching lines`). A line is left out when the signature column already shows all of it, wherever it is in the block (the lines of a signature that spans several, or the signature line below a Rust item's attributes or doc comments), so the snippet is `null` when the signature is the only match. A line that says more than the signature stays in, such as a decorator, the start of an arrow function's body or a body on the same line. To read the whole block, open the file at `lineStart`–`lineEnd`. Under the table, `help` lines report files that were skipped, degraded (syntax errors, too deep to parse) or read lossily (invalid UTF-8), a partial result, hit lines that were cut, and a query with no positive terms.

## Writing a query

| You write | It means |
| --- | --- |
| `format price` | Code that mentions either word, ranked by how well it matches |
| `"format price"` | The exact phrase |
| `+cart` | Files must mention `cart` |
| `-Button` | Skip files that mention `Button` |
| `regex:use[A-Z]\w+` | Lines matching a regular expression |
| `regex:"a pattern with spaces"` | A regular expression with whitespace, quoted. `+` and `-` work in front of `regex:` too |
| `--exact` | Treat the whole query as one literal, operators and quotes included |

Matching ignores case. A `-term` removes whole files, not single results. If one query mixes terms, `+cart -Button` finds code in files that mention `cart` but never `Button`:

```
$ monokl search "+cart -Button" .
search[2]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,rank,finalScore}:
  src/hooks/useCart.ts,11,25,function,null,function useCart(),"12: const [items, setItems] = useState<CartItem[]>([]);\n14: const addItem = (item: CartItem): ValidationResult => {",1,1.359319
  src/hooks/useCart.ts,5,9,interface,null,null,"5: export interface CartItem {",2,0.904979
```

## Options

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--max-results N` | 50 | Most results to print |
| `--max-tokens N` | 20,000 | Most estimated tokens (one per three bytes) across the printed rows. The cut is a prefix in rank order and the output says how many rows were cut |
| `--exact` | off | Treat the whole query as one literal term, operators and quotes included |
| `--tests` | off | Also search test files: anything under `test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/` or `spec/`, and `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` in any searchable extension (`ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `mts`, `cts`). Also searches Rust files named `tests.rs`, `test.rs`, `*_tests.rs` or `*_test.rs` (the usual out-of-line `mod tests;`) and Rust items under `#[cfg(test)]` or `#[test]` |
| `--no-ignore` | off | Also search hidden files and files that `.gitignore` or `.ignore` exclude, in the search path or its parent directories |
| `--language L` | all | Search one language only: `typescript`, `javascript` or `rust`, chosen by file extension: `.ts .tsx .mts .cts`, `.js .jsx .mjs .cjs` or `.rs`. Any other value is a usage error (exit 2) that lists these three |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | 30 | Stop after this many seconds and print what was found so far. `0` means no limit. Fractions are accepted (`0.5`) |

## Limits

- **Time.** When `--timeout` expires the output says `partial result: 30 s timeout expired after analyzing 120 of 900 files` (or `searching`, when the text search itself ran out of time). The exit code is still 0. A partial result is the only output that can differ between runs, because which files are reached depends on how fast the machine is. At least one batch of files is always processed, so a very small timeout still returns something. A `-term` exclusion applies only to the files that were reached. The directory walk that lists the files is not interrupted.
- **File size.** A file over 4 MiB is not read. The output says `2 files skipped: over 4 MiB: a.ts, b.ts`. Source that large is generated or bundled; reading it costs about 2.5 times its size in memory.

content.content:
Member questions use the same file format with the symbol cell written `member:name`: the answer is a method,
constructor, accessor or arrow-function property declared on an indented line inside a class. The script re-checks that
line with rg and scores them on their own line, apart from the top-level questions. A member question is a hit when the
answer file is in monokl's first `--top` files and the member's declaration line is in the output; the gate is
`--min-member-recall`.

Each repository has a language (the optional fourth column of rg-compare.repos, default `ts`). A `rust` repository is
searched with `*.rs`, its declarations are `fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|macro_rules!` at the start of a
line (optional `pub`, `pub(crate)`), and its members are `fn` and `const` on an indented line inside an `impl` or
`trait` block. `tests/` directories are test files; `#[cfg(test)]` modules are test code for the analyzer, but this
script works on whole files and cannot split them, so a `mod tests` is skipped when sampling and test code inside
source files still counts as source here. monokl runs without `--language`, which searches every registered language,
so no flag is passed. Rust rows (identifiers, questions and members together) are scored apart from the TypeScript
gates and gated by `--min-rust-recall`, which defaults to 0.9 now that the analyzer ships. A Rust repository that monokl
cannot search yet scores 0 hits, which the report states.
    parser.add_argument("--terms", type=int, default=25, help="identifiers sampled per repository")
    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=3, help="a declaration must appear within this many files")
    parser.add_argument("--min-recall", type=float, default=0.95, help="fail when the share of hits is lower")
    parser.add_argument("--min-question-recall", type=float, default=0.9,
                        help="fail when the share of questions with the answer file in the top files is lower")
    parser.add_argument("--min-member-recall", type=float, default=0.9,
                        help="fail when the share of member questions with the answer file in the top files and the "
                             "member's declaration in the output is lower")
    parser.add_argument("--min-rust-recall", type=float, default=0.9,
                        help="fail when the share of Rust hits (identifiers, questions and members pooled) is lower; "
                             "0.9 by default")
    parser.add_argument("--min-heldout-recall", type=float, default=0.9,
                        help="fail when the share of held-out questions with the answer file in the top files is lower; "
| `just rg-compare [--terms N] [--min-recall R]` | Whether `monokl search` puts a symbol's declaration in the top files, and how much output it costs against `rg -n`, on pinned public repos, plus 18 multi-word questions with known answers (`scripts/rg-compare.questions`, gated by `--min-question-recall`), 36 held-out questions on fastify, trpc and date-fns scored apart (`--min-heldout-recall`, `--min-heldout-member-recall`, both 0.9), and Rust rows on pinned `fd` (24 pooled, gated by `--min-rust-recall`, 0.9) (on demand, needs network) |

---
monokl: minor
---

Blocks carry the byte span they cover and the position of the block that encloses them, so later stages can tell blocks apart by where they are and not by their text.

- **Span.** `CodeBlock::span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. Offsets count bytes of the text the analyzer received, which is the lossy UTF-8 decoding of a file with invalid bytes.
- **Parent.** `CodeBlock::parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`. It is set exactly when `parent` is, for the members of a class, object literal, `impl`, trait or inline module.
- **No change to results.** Nothing reads either field yet: `monokl search` output and the harness scores are unchanged.

**Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has two new public fields. Code that builds one must set `span` and `parent_index`.

---
monokl: minor
---

**`monokl search` prints less by default.** The default output is the rows that matter, with one snippet line each, so an answer costs about a tenth of the bytes. On the 222 rows of the harness the median output falls from 10,012 to 902 bytes and the 90th percentile from 13,351 to 3,207, and the share of questions whose expected declaration is in the first 3 rows stays at 204 of 222.

- **Relevance cut.** A row is kept when its `finalScore` is at least 0.3 times the top row's (`--min-score FRACTION`, `0` turns the cut off). The first 3 rows are always kept when that many exist. `--max-results` is the cap on top of that, now 15 by default (was 50), and it wins over the floor of 3. `--min-score` takes 0 to 1; anything else is a usage error (exit 2).
- **Snippet.** Each row shows its first matching line and counts the rest (`...and 2 more matching lines`). `--snippet-lines N` shows 0 to 3 lines (3 is the old snippet). `0` prints no snippet, so a variable or type row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text.
- **Help line.** When rows were cut the help names the flag that brings them back: `showing 4 of 37; --min-score 0 or --max-results N for more, or refine with +term/-term`. It names `--max-tokens N` when the tokens ran out first. There is no `--offset` yet.
- **Harness.** Each set loses at most one question: members 15/16 to 14/16 and Rust 22/24 to 21/24, so `--min-member-recall` and `--min-rust-recall` now default to 0.85. Search time is unchanged.
- **Not measured.** Whether a model finds the answer in the leaner rows, and what snippet lines 2 and 3 are worth when an agent reads for context instead of answering in one turn.

**Breaking:** The default output changed: at most 15 rows (was 50), none below 0.3 times the top score except the first 3, and one snippet line per row (was up to 3). `SearchResponse` has a new public field, `blocks_cut_by_relevance`, `Budget` has a new public field, `min_score` (and no longer implements `Eq`), and `render_search` and `search_row_texts` take a `SearchView` and a snippet length. The truncation help line is reworded.

**Action:** To get the earlier output, run `monokl search <query> --min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`. Code that builds a `SearchResponse` or a `Budget`, or calls `render_search` or `search_row_texts`, must pass the new values: `Budget::default()` carries the new defaults, and `SearchView::default()` the new snippet length.
